title: His wife Peggy and the uncommercial label
summary: Peggy the nurse kept him in line, while the illness cut him off and labeled him uncommercial.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: I guess you were lucky in the other respect, that Peggy, your wife, was a nurse.

Yes. She'd give me the back of the hand, she wouldn't let you feel sorry for yourself. That kept me, as far as the music business is concerned, probably from making the connections that might have lead to further things. It locked me into a certain area and I never have seen to have gotten out of that.
I got a reputation at that point for being uncommercial, which is the kiss of death. They sent me off to their own special
Siberia through the years, and I never lived that one down either, even though it's no longer true.
Although if you are doing Broadway shows, you can't be totally stigmatized in that regard.
I don't think they see me at all--the people involved in shows don't see me beyond shows. They don't know anything else, they don't know anything else exists.
That's true of a lot of areas of the music business. I have found that everything has their own little cubicle that they're interested in.
